section_title: What is the good news that makes Jerusalem sing?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength, O Zion! Put on your garments of splendor, O Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you. 2 Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem. Remove the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion. 3 For this is what the LORD says: “You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed.”

4 For this is what the Lord GOD says: “At first My people went down to Egypt to live, then Assyria oppressed them without cause. 5 And now what have I here? declares the LORD. For My people have been taken without cause; those who rule them taunt, declares the LORD, and My name is blasphemed continually all day long. 6 Therefore My people will know My name; therefore they will know on that day that I am He who speaks. Here I am!”

7 How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!” 8 Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices, together they shout for joy. For every eye will see when the LORD returns to Zion. 9 Break forth in joy, sing together, O ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem. 10 The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations; all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.

11 Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; come out from it, purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD. 12 For you will not leave in a hurry nor flee in haste, for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard.

context_lines: Jerusalem is called to rise from the dust, remove her chains and put on garments of splendor. The opening picture changes her condition from captive humiliation to the dignity of a holy city. Her redemption will not depend on someone raising a purchase price.

The Lord recalls the people’s stay in Egypt and their oppression by Assyria. Now His people are taken away and His name is continually dishonored. He promises that they will know the One who speaks and acts for them.

A messenger announces peace, salvation and the reign of their God. Watchmen lift their voices together, and even the ruined city is called to sing. The Lord has comforted and redeemed His people, and the ends of the earth will see His salvation.

The departure requires purity, especially for those carrying the Lord’s vessels. It will be a secure departure rather than a panicked escape: the Lord goes before them, and the God of Israel guards their rear.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/isaiah/52.htm) connects the promised redemption with the return from Babylon and with the Messiah’s fuller saving work. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/isaiah/52.htm) likewise relates the announcement of God’s reign to Christ and to those who carry His good news.

Both read the call to leave uncleanness as part of the freedom God gives. The messengers bring news of His rescue, while the departing people are called to leave the pollutions of captivity behind. His protection accompanies the journey.
god_plan_lines: [Romans 10:13–17](https://biblehub.com/bsb/romans/10.htm) directly uses the announcement about beautiful feet to explain the sending of gospel messengers. People need to hear about Christ, and messengers must be sent to tell them. The good news of God’s salvation is carried outward through that work.

[Second Corinthians 6:14–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/2_corinthians/6.htm) also takes up the command to come out and touch nothing unclean. Paul applies it to the church’s allegiance to the living God rather than idols. Isaiah’s language therefore serves both the spread of the gospel and the call for God’s people to live faithfully in response.
